newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta, Swissair, Sabena mull joint freighter.
newsitem.headline: Delta, Swissair, Sabena mull joint freighter.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said it is discussing operating a joint Europe-U.S. freighter service with partner airlines Swissair and Sabena.

Danita Waterfall, Delta's regional director cargo sales and services Europe, told Reuters in an interview: "We are trying to make the most of our alliances. In the past the code-shares were for passenger benefits only."
Delta, Swissair, Sabena and Austrian Airlines have gained anti-immunity trust from U.S. authorities for their Atlantic Excellence passenger code-sharing agreement
Waterfall said: "This year we are looking at opportunities for freighter-sharing. We have a couple of routes where we think we could justify a freighter."
But it was too early to say which routes would come into question since a decision was likely first at the end of the fiscal year next June, she said.
Regular high-level meetings between the cargo vice-presidents of the partner airlines are taking place, Waterfall disclosed.
Options under discussion also include blocked or mutual use of space, joint handling arrangements, warehousing arrangements and sales staff, she added.
Waterfall said: "We are also working with Swissair and Sabena on connecting our systems a little, on sales and reservations." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
